feedback.answered: Exploration 7787ec32a33f4ae0a2f558ac34428ecd executed a three-node public-API history: implicit removal entry index 5 was committed and applied; transfer target 2 was installed before Advance; one emitted TimeoutNow was dropped. At timeout and after thirty additional reliably delivered tick rounds, leader 1 remained term 2 with commit/applied/last index 5 and outgoing count 3. Network queue, leader Ready, storage/apply pending work were empty in emitted diagnostics. The no-transfer control exited at index 6; later ordinary proposal in the overlap case enabled exit at index 7. Public Status AutoLeave=false is not evidence of live AutoLeave loss: getStatus calls Config.Clone, whose returned literal omits AutoLeave. Preserve this independent copy discrepancy and use live fields when checking continuation.
remaining: Formal execution must follow fixed inputs and an independent correlated predicate; exploration is not Evidence.
Full recurrence needs all relevant nodes, queues, timers and callback state, not just printed business fields.
The Config.Clone omission is a separate sourced semantic discrepancy; no live protocol mutation or external consequence has been established from it.

question.question: After an implicit joint configuration has been committed and applied, does raft retain an automatic exit continuation when the appliedTo proposal is rejected by an in-progress leader transfer which subsequently times out, while the original leader and both quorums remain available and all existing work is drained?
question.importance: Failure could leave the obsolete outgoing quorum required indefinitely until unrelated application work or leadership change, impairing membership completion and availability after intended removal. This is a scoped continuation question, not a demonstrated safety failure or a numeric deadline claim.
contexts: Synchronous RawNode API with persistence and ordered configuration application before Advance
Implicit joint membership change retaining current leader and transfer target
Finite loss of TimeoutNow followed by fully delivered heartbeats and responses, no new client proposals

Control: same configuration with no overlapping transfer; rescue: later ordinary entry if the quiescent suffix leaves joint state unchanged

No tick deadline is specified for configuration completion.
Exploration shows an unrelated ordinary proposal allows exit, confirming a remaining application-progress trigger; this does not show that callers owe that proposal.

question.trigger_rationale: appliedTo alone initiates automatic exit, and explicitly permits Step to reject it during transfer. abortLeaderTransfer only clears leadTransferee. Advance generates application responses only for nonempty committed batches. This difference warrants a small real-cluster schedule rather than repeating an isolated guard test.

obligation.description: For a committed and applied implicit joint transition, Raft must retain automatic continuation to the final configuration when a leader and both quorums are available and caller-required ticking, transport, persistence and application continue. A rejected internal exit proposal during a transient leadership transfer must not leave the transition permanently dependent on an unrelated new client proposal after the transfer has ended.

scope.description: Implicit joint exit with the current leader retained as a voter, a transient failed transfer, no ongoing failures and fair servicing of all implementation-requested work.
assumptions: Configuration entry is genuinely committed and applied through the normal interface.
Transport may lose finitely many messages, then delivers all generated messages; local Ready work is processed reliably in order.
Stable available leader and sufficient incoming/outgoing voters; no infinite elections or failed storage.
No obligation for a fresh unrelated user command or manually proposed explicit exit is imposed on implicit-transition callers.
excluded: No claim that configuration proposals must be admitted initially.
No crash/restart, Byzantine behavior, explicit joint transitions or arbitrary membership changes.
No claim of consensus safety failure or measured downstream availability outage.

grounding.derivation: ConfChangeTransitionJointImplicit specifies that raft transitions out automatically by proposing a zero change, whereas JointExplicit assigns that proposal to the application. tracker.Config.AutoLeave repeats that ownership when possible. appliedTo implements the automatic proposal and documents transfer rejection plus an expected later advance. Generic proposal retry duties do not transfer this internal automatic task to the caller. The responsibility is eventual continuation under available quorums, not completion after a fixed number of ticks.
grounding.applicability: Actual committed/applied implicit transition and fully serviced stable-leader suffix after a finite failed transfer. A violation requires a closed non-progress execution suffix or equivalently sourced proof that required future triggers cannot occur, beyond finite non-completion.
alternatives: A successful leadership change or later applied ordinary entry can initiate exit; those rescue paths do not establish automatic continuation in a stable idle workload.

associations.rationale: This is the implementation-owned initiator of the specified automatic transition.

bindings.description: Consumes applied progress and AutoLeave to attempt the internal empty proposal, including the transfer rejection branch.
